first_divergence.exact_span: draft-v3.tex lines 133-137: "A finite maximal endpoint makes the next step exact. If \(T_*<\infty\), the endpoint continuation criterion requires \[\sup_{0<t<T_*}\|u(t)\|_{L^3}=\infty.\]"
first_divergence.mechanism: The preceding Zeno paragraph establishes that a proposed sequence of shrinking viscous response intervals can fit below a finite terminal time, but it does not establish a maximal-lifespan contradiction or identify \(L^3\). The section had just singled out \(\dot H^{1/2}\) as critical. The global \(L^3\) continuation criterion then appears as an external theorem with no bridge showing why it is the next necessary object, so the temporal-row argument begins from a fact the reader could not infer from the developed chain.
first_divergence.repair_constraint: Keep the finite endpoint assumption live as a contradiction hypothesis and earn the change from the \(\dot H^{1/2}\) scale to \(L^3\): introduce \(L^3\) as another scale-invariant norm and state the continuation implication that bounded \(L^3\) up to \(T_*\) permits extension; only then take its contrapositive to force \(L^3\) escape and begin temporal integration.
